Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the load that calls for a hire, the weeks before you hire, the hours after which overtime starts, the overtime multiplier and the overload hours.
Check Team, Crews and Contract Hours: these small tables drive pay, capacity and overtime. A crew is the cleaners who work together on a job, and a labour hour is one cleaner working for one hour.
Fill Timesheets each week with the start, finish, break and road time. The hours worked, the overtime hours, the day pay and the day check fill in by themselves.
Write every approved overtime on Overtime Log with the reason and who approved it; the cost at your multiplier is calculated.
Keep Leave and Absence and Shift Swaps current so you always know who covers whom, and read Overload Alerts before a long day.
Read Capacity by Week: utilization is the share of paid crew hours that are booked on jobs. A crew above your hire level for several weeks is the signal to hire.
Track candidates on Hiring Pipeline, courses on Training Records and scores on Performance Reviews; the check columns warn you about slow candidates, expired training and low ratings.
Use Pay for the monthly pay of each cleaner with the bonus, Bonus Rules for the levels, Kit Issued for what each cleaner holds and Crew Labour Cost for the labour cost per job.

Use the 14 calculators when you plan: crew hours, utilization, growth, the hire trigger, pay, overtime, labour cost, break-even, leave cover, bonus, crew size, new hire cost, travel pay and a finish-time grid.
Read the Crews and Pay Dashboard and Charts every week: hours, utilization, pay, overtime, leave, hiring and training.
Payroll, tax, leave pay and employment rules differ by place: check your own local rules before you use any sample wording.
